records.title: Prices for construction sand in Gasabo skyrocket
records.titleEn: Prices for construction sand in Gasabo skyrocket
records.location: Kigali City, Gasabo District (Rusine, Bumbogo, Jabana areas; Nduba and Kimironko sectors named)
records.summary: Gasabo District authorities suspended sand mining across the district after finding miners operating illegally, pending environmental impact assessments; the article notes local regulations bar sand excavation in wetlands. A New Times mini survey found big crystal sand rose from Rwf50,000 to Rwf75,000 per truckload and small crystal sand from Rwf45,000 to Rwf55,000. District environment officer Peter Barigye said operators had failed to meet minimum requirements set in 2008. A truck driver blamed higher transport costs because sand was now ferried from Bugesera. Nduba Sector said its suspension followed rice farmers' claims that rain-washed sand deposits were burying cultivable soil.

records.titleEn: Gasabo sand miners demand clear policies from leaders
records.location: Kigali City, Gasabo District, Kinyinya Sector
records.summary: Sand miners in Gasabo say unpredictable regulation by Kigali City threatens their business as demand for construction sand grows. Miner Ferdinand Ishimwe said his Kinyinya site, exploiting two hectares and employing some 40 labourers, was closed four times within a year. A labourer with eight years in the trade said he earns Rwf4,000 a day on average. Kinyinya sector executive secretary Remon Berabahizi said the sector, with 15 sites, hosts most of the sand mining Kigali relies on, that many operators leave holes unrehabilitated, and that the sector collects Rwf500,000 per day on average in taxes from sand miners.

records.title: Everything comes from something: A geographic photo analysis of sand extraction and usage in Rwanda’s rapidly growing economy
records.titleEn: Everything comes from something: A geographic photo analysis of sand extraction and usage in Rwanda's rapidly growing economy
records.dateEvidence: No publication date found on the source page
records.location: Nyabugogo River near Kigali; Rusine River; a tributary of the river spelled 'Mukuwunga' on the Northern-Western Province border; Rutongo Mines area
records.summary: A photo essay by McGill University geographer Mette Bendixen, based on fieldwork photos from June 2023 and 2024, documents artisanal sand extraction in Rwanda. On the Nyabugogo River near Kigali, men ranging from teenagers to their 40s stand hip-deep to dig sand from the riverbed, stockpiling it on platforms for dump trucks; riverbank erosion and collapse are described as common. On the Rusine River women crush stone while only men extract sand, and sand bags carried on the head weigh over 30 kilos. The author argues national housing plans omit sand, gravel and crushed stone.
records.limitations: Photo essay rather than a quantitative study; no publication date is printed on the page (DOI suggests 2025). The essay spells Nyabugogo as Nyabogogo and names a tributary of a 'Mukuwunga' River (possibly the Mukungwa, not tagged); districts are not named. English translation of the headline awaits native-language review.
